images.title: Tens, hundreds and thousands in 2,745
images.purpose: Show that dropping the digits on the right tells how many thousands, hundreds or tens a number holds, and what is left over each time.
images.composition: The number 2,745 at the top left, then three rows of the same four digit boxes, each row colouring more of the left digits. The counts and the left over amounts are written to the right of each row.
images.exact_structure: Plain white 16:9 canvas. TOP LEFT: the number 2,745 in large type. Just under it, a header row of four small labels over four columns, left to right: Th, H, T, O. Below the header are exactly three rows, one under the other. Each row is made of four square digit boxes in the same four columns, holding the digits 2, 7, 4, 5 from left to right (12 digit boxes in all; the digit 2 is under Th, 7 under H, 4 under T, 5 under O). Row 1: box 1 is filled teal #0072B2 with a white digit; boxes 2, 3 and 4 are white with a grey #6B7280 outline and grey digit. Row 2: boxes 1 and 2 are teal; boxes 3 and 4 are grey. Row 3: boxes 1, 2 and 3 are teal; box 4 is grey. To the right of each row, on one line, a bold teal count followed by a smaller grey left over: row 1 reads 2 thousands then 745 left; row 2 reads 27 hundreds then 45 left; row 3 reads 274 tens then 5 left. Nothing else is drawn.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The digits to the left of a place say how many thousands, hundreds or tens the number holds, and the digits on the right are what is left over.
images.description: The number 2,745 shown three times, with the digits that count the thousands, the hundreds and the tens coloured, and the left over part written beside each.
images.context: Starting point is the chapter's note about how many tens, hundreds and thousands a number holds. The number is the plan's own 2,745 from the concept's worked example. The rows match the counts 2 thousands, 27 hundreds and 274 tens, with 745, 45 and 5 left. The notes of 500 and the form 200 Tens + 745 Ones are not drawn.
images.teaching_notes: Ask first: how many tens in 2,745, is it the tens digit 4? Then cover the last digit and read the rest. Misconception M_TENS_COUNT: the number of tens is 274, not the tens digit.

image_decisions.why: Three rows of the same digits, each colouring more of the left part, show how counting tens, hundreds and thousands works.
